assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water soaks up lots of heat without getting hot fast! It circulates inside the engine, picks up the heat, and releases it at the radiator.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes water circulating and carrying heat away, which is a real-world heat-transfer situation, but it never names or identifies conduction, convection, or radiation, nor does it present the example as an advantageous/disadvantageous instance of any of these mechanisms. It does not directly teach the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water soaks up lots of heat without getting hot fast!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on the idea that water absorbs heat without a large temperature rise, which relates to heat vs. temperature, but it does not explain the difference between heat and temperature. It only states a property of water, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
How does water cool a car engine?

Water soaks up lots of heat without getting hot fast! It circulates inside the engine, picks up the heat, and releases it at the radiator.
copy.tl:
Paano pinapalamig ng tubig ang makina ng kotse?

Kayang sumipsip ng tubig ng maraming init nang hindi mabilis umiinit! Umiikot ito sa loob ng makina, kinukuha ang init, at inilalabas sa radiator.
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagpabugnaw sa tubig sa makina sa awto?

Makasuyop ang tubig og daghang init nga dili kalit moinit! Moliyok kini sa sulod sa makina, mokuha sa init, ug mopagawas niini sa radiator.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it can double its numbers in just a few days, quickly covering a whole lake or river's surface
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Fast vegetative spread is yield, not a description of pollination, seed production, or plant propagation as methods.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it can double its numbers in just a few days, quickly covering a whole lake
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the ecosystem's population growth slows down as it gets closer to the carrying capacity
assignedReviews.reason: Rapid doubling is population growth, not growth slowing as it nears carrying capacity.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: quickly covering a whole lake or river's surface
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe the possible effects of human activities, such as deforestation, pollution, and introduction of invasive species, on living things in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: Covering a lake is invasive-adjacent, but the card does not describe human activities such as deforestation, pollution, or introduction of invasive species.

copy.en:
How fast does water hyacinth spread?

Super fast — it can double its numbers in just a few days, quickly covering a whole lake or river's surface!
copy.tl:
Gaano kabilis dumami ang water hyacinth?

Napakabilis — kaya nitong magdoble ang dami sa loob lang ng ilang araw, kayang matakpan ang buong lawa o ilog!
copy.bis:
Unsa kapaspas modaghan ang water hyacinth?

Paspas kaayo — mahimo niining doblehon ang gidaghanon sulod lang sa pipila ka adlaw, matabunan dayon ang tibuok linaw o suba!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the water pressure at the faucet is higher when the tank is higher up
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a pressure phenomenon caused by the height of a water column, which is ultimately due to gravity, but it never identifies gravity as a non-contact force or explains the force concept. It only states an everyday observation about water pressure, so it does not directly teach the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the water pressure at the faucet is higher when the tank is higher up
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The competency asks to observe and describe the effects of gravity on the motion of an object. The card is about water pressure, not about the motion of an object under gravity. It does not describe any object's motion, so it is only tangentially related to gravity's effects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the water pressure at the faucet is higher when the tank is higher up
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces act between objects and can be measured
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about identifying that forces act between objects and can be measured. The card does not mention forces, measurement, or the interaction between objects. It only states a relationship between tank height and water pressure, which is not directly about force identification or measurement.

copy.en:
Why are water tanks placed on high roofs?

In homes with an overhead water tank, the water pressure at the faucet is higher when the tank is higher up! That's why they are placed on roofs.
copy.tl:
Bakit inilalagay ang mga water tank sa mataas na bubong?

Sa mga bahay na may overhead water tank, mas mataas ang water pressure sa gripo kapag mas mataas ang tank! Kaya inilalagay sila sa bubong.
copy.bis:
Nganong gibutang ang mga water tank sa taas nga atop?

Sa mga balay nga adunay overhead water tank, mas taas ang water pressure sa gripo kon mas taas ang tank! Mao nga gibutang sila sa atop.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water cools the surfaces and removes heat, so the fire cannot spread to those areas!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how important types of chemical reactions, such as combustion, acids on metals, acids on carbonates, photosynthesis, and respiration, relate to or impact the natural and built environments using information from secondary sources
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions fire (combustion) but only describes heat removal by water, not the chemical reaction of combustion or how combustion relates to environments. It does not explain any chemical reaction or its environmental impact, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water cools the surfaces and removes heat, so the fire cannot spread to those areas!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about firefighting and heat transfer, not about uniform or non-uniform mixtures such as solutions and suspensions. No mixture concept is taught, so this code is unrelated.

copy.en:
Why do firefighters spray water on surfaces near a fire?

Water cools the surfaces and removes heat, so the fire cannot spread to those areas!
copy.tl:
Bakit nag-i-spray ng tubig ang mga bumbero sa mga surface malapit sa apoy?

Pinapalamig ng tubig ang mga surface at inaalis nito ang init, kaya hindi na kumakalat ang apoy sa mga lugar na iyon!
copy.bis:
Ngano mag-spray ug tubig ang mga bombero sa mga surface duol sa kalayo?

Ang tubig nagpabugnaw sa mga surface ug nagkuha sa kainit, mao nga dili na mokatap ang kalayo sa mga lugar nga kana!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A floating part bobs up and down with each wave, spinning a generator that makes electricity!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that waves carry energy from a source to a receiver
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a wave-energy converter, an application of wave energy, but does not explicitly teach that waves carry energy from a source to a receiver. It is an example of wave energy use, not direct instruction of the concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A floating part bobs up and down with each wave, spinning a generator that makes electricity!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how increased societal uses of renewable energies could mitigate the effects of global climate change, including how the Philippines could make better use of its plentiful natural resources
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows a renewable energy technology (wave power) but does not explain how increased societal uses of renewable energies mitigate climate change or how the Philippines could use its resources. It is a specific example without the required explanation.

copy.en: A floating part bobs up and down with each wave, spinning a generator that makes electricity!
copy.tl: May lumulutang na bahagi na umaakyat-bumababa kasabay ng alon, na nagpapaikot ng generator para gumawa ng kuryente!
copy.bis: Adunay naglutaw nga bahin nga mosaka-mokunsad sa matag balod, nga motuyok sa generator aron mohimo og kuryente!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They use sound speed and echoes! By timing how long a sound takes to bounce back
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card uses sound travel and echo timing for sonar distance measurement, but it does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred in everyday situations such as a ringing bell or hearing noises. It only assumes sound travels and reflects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: By timing how long a sound takes to bounce back, ships use sonar to find the exact distance
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure accurately the distance and time when things move using simple equipment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions timing and distance, but it does not involve measuring distance and time of moving things with simple equipment. Sonar is an indirect echo-based measurement, not the guided measurement of moving objects addressed by this competency.

copy.en:
How do ships measure distance underwater?

They use sound speed and echoes! By timing how long a sound takes to bounce back, ships use sonar to find the exact distance.
copy.tl:
Paano sumusukat ng layo ang mga barko?

Gamit ang bilis ng tunog at echo! Sa pag-time kung gaano katagal bumalik ang tunog, ginagamit ng sonar sa barko para makuha ang layo.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagsukod sa gilay-on sa mga barko?

Pinaagi sa kapaspas sa tingog ug echo! Sa pag-time kung unsa ka dugay mibalik ang tingog, gigamit sa sonar sa barko para makuha ang gilay-on.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Do we use all the oxygen we breathe in?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card only discusses oxygen in inhaled and exhaled air. It does not identify or describe the nose, windpipe, or lungs, nor how the respiratory system works, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the air we breathe out still has some oxygen
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on respiration by noting that not all inhaled oxygen is used, but it does not describe the process of photosynthesis or respiration, nor identify raw materials and products. It is only loosely related to the competency.

copy.en:
Do we use all the oxygen we breathe in?

Nope! We don't use all the oxygen we breathe in, so the air we breathe out still has some oxygen!
copy.tl:
Ginagamit ba natin ang lahat ng oxygen na hininga?

Hindi! Hindi natin ginagamit ang lahat ng oxygen na hininga, kaya may oxygen pa rin sa hangin na inilalabas natin!
copy.bis:
Nagamit ba nato ang tanang oksiheno nga atong ginhinga?

Dili! Dili nato magamit ang tanang oksiheno nga atong ginhinga, mao nga ang hangin nga atong gibuga aduna pay oksiheno!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Separate water or sugar molecules are held together by weak intermolecular forces
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses intermolecular forces between molecules, but does not describe matter as having mass and taking up space, which is the specific skill of G5-M-1.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Separate water or sugar molecules are held together by weak intermolecular forces
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions molecules but does not identify or describe the three states of matter (solids, liquids, gases), so it does not directly support G5-M-2.

copy.en: Separate water or sugar molecules are held together by weak intermolecular forces, which are gentle attractions between molecules, much weaker than the bonds inside each molecule.
copy.tl: Ang magkakahiwalay na water o sugar molecules ay pinagdidikit ng mahihinang intermolecular forces, na mga banayad na atraksyon sa pagitan ng mga molecules, mas mahina kaysa sa bonds sa loob ng bawat molecule.
copy.bis: Ang bulag nga water o sugar molecules gihuptan sa mga huyang nga intermolecular forces, nga mga hinay nga atraksyon tali sa mga molecules, mas huyang kay sa bonds sa sulod sa matag molecule.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It carries small instruments high up to measure the heat, moisture, and wind in the upper air.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use weather instruments to measure and record some of the characteristics of weather during a school day
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions instruments measuring weather characteristics, but it is about a weather balloon measuring upper air, not about using weather instruments to measure and record weather during a school day. It does not support the specific skill of using instruments in a school-day context.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: measure the heat, moisture, and wind in the upper air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card names heat, moisture, and wind, which are weather characteristics, but it does not identify the basic characteristics used to describe weather (air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, cloud cover) in a general sense. It focuses on upper-air measurement by a balloon, not on identifying weather descriptors.

copy.en:
What flies high into the sky to measure the upper air?

A weather balloon! It carries small instruments high up to measure the heat, moisture, and wind in the upper air.
copy.tl:
Ano ang lumilipad nang mataas sa himpapawid para sukatin ang upper air?

Isang weather balloon! Nagdadala ito ng maliliit na instrumento pataas para sukatin ang heat, moisture, at wind sa upper air.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang molupad nga taas sa kalangitan aron sukdon ang upper air?

Usa ka weather balloon! Nagdala kini og gagmayng himan pataas aron sukdon ang heat, moisture, ug wind sa upper air.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Falling water levels in rivers and dams are early signs of an approaching drought!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some effects of weather disturbances that occur in or near the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions drought, which could be considered a weather-related disturbance, but it describes early signs (falling water levels) rather than effects of weather disturbances. It does not describe impacts of a disturbance on communities or environment as the competency requires.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PAGASA and water utilities monitor these levels to plan water conservation.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions PAGASA monitoring water levels, but it does not involve examining a local weather chart, making interpretations about local weather, or describing/practicing safety precautions for poor or extreme weather. The monitoring is for drought planning, not weather chart interpretation or safety precautions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Falling water levels in rivers and dams are early signs of an approaching drought!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in the weather can affect daily activities and explain how some types of weather can be dangerous for people
assignedReviews.reason: The card relates to drought, a weather condition, but it does not describe how changes in weather affect daily activities or explain how weather can be dangerous. It only states a sign of drought and monitoring, not effects on people or danger.

copy.en: Falling water levels in rivers and dams are early signs of an approaching drought! PAGASA and water utilities monitor these levels to plan water conservation.
copy.tl: Ang pagbaba ng antas ng tubig sa mga ilog at dam ay maagang senyales ng paparating na tagtuyot! Binabantayan ito ng PAGASA at water utilities para magplano ng water conservation.
copy.bis: Ang pagbaba sa antas sa tubig sa mga suba ug dam usa sa sayo nga senyales sa paparapit nga hulaw! Gimonitor sa PAGASA ug water utilities kini aron magplano sa water conservation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They use data from satellites, radar, weather stations, and powerful computers!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how meteorologists make forecasts using data sources and computer models. It does not address examining a local weather chart, making simple interpretations of local weather, or describing/practicing safety precautions for poor or extreme weather. The content is only broadly related to weather.

copy.en:
How do meteorologists make weather forecasts?

They use data from satellites, radar, weather stations, and powerful computers! Computer models process millions of data points.
copy.tl:
Paano gumagawa ng mga hula sa panahon ang mga meteorolohista?

Gumagamit sila ng datos mula sa satellite, radar, weather station, at malalaking computer! Ang computer model ay kino-compute ang milyun-milyong datos.
copy.bis:
Unsaon paghimo sa mga hula sa panahon sa mga meteorolohista?

Naggamit sila sa datos gikan sa satellite, radar, weather station, ug gamhanan nga kompyuter! Ang computer model nagproseso sa milyon-milyong datos.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: frost and near-freezing conditions
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions temperature (frost, near-freezing) and wind (amihan), which are weather characteristics, but it does not teach students to identify the basic characteristics used to describe weather (air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, cloud cover). It is a specific fact about frost at high elevations, not an instructional support for identifying weather characteristics.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: strong amihan
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different seasons in the Philippines and suggest activities that are appropriate for each season
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a season-related wind (amihan) and cold conditions, but it does not describe the different seasons in the Philippines or suggest activities appropriate for each season. It only gives a specific weather phenomenon tied to one season, not a description of seasons or appropriate activities.

copy.en:
Can it ever get cold enough for frost in the Philippines?

Yes! During strong amihan, the highest peaks of Mount Pulag and other mountains experience frost and near-freezing conditions, even though snow isn't normal here.
copy.tl:
Pwede bang lumamig nang sobra para magkaroon ng frost sa Pilipinas?

Oo! Sa panahon ng malakas na amihan, ang pinakamataas na peaks ng Mount Pulag at iba pang bundok ay nakararanas ng frost at near-freezing conditions.
copy.bis:
Pwede bang molamig og nindot para naay frost sa Pilipinas?

Oo! Sa panahon sa kusog nga amihan, ang pinakataas nga peaks sa Mount Pulag ug ubang bundok makasinati sa frost ug near-freezing conditions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because obstacles like trees and buildings change the wind flow and heat!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use weather instruments to measure and record some of the characteristics of weather during a school day
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why weather stations are placed in open fields, mentioning wind and heat, but does not instruct on using weather instruments to measure and record weather characteristics during a school day. It provides background rationale rather than direct support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because obstacles like trees and buildings change the wind flow and heat!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions wind and heat, which are weather characteristics, but does not identify the basic characteristics used to describe weather (air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, cloud cover). It only gives a reason for station placement, not instruction on identifying weather characteristics.

copy.en:
Why do weather stations sit in open fields, away from trees and buildings?

Because obstacles like trees and buildings change the wind flow and heat! In an open area, the readings of the real surrounding weather are much more accurate.
copy.tl:
Bakit inilalagay ang weather station sa bukas na parang, malayo sa mga puno at gusali?

Dahil kung may humaharang, mababago ang daloy ng hangin at ang init na nasusukat! Sa bukas na lugar, mas tama ang sukat ng totoong panahon sa paligid.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga ang weather station gibutang sa bukas nga uma, layo sa mga kahoy ug building?

Tungod kay kung adunay babag, mausab ang dagan sa hangin ug ang init nga masukod! Sa bukas nga dapit, mas saktong masukod ang tinuod nga panahon sa palibot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PAGASA gives local names to typhoons
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal issued by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geological and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA)
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that PAGASA assigns local names to typhoons from a rotating list, but the competency requires describing weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal. The card does not address warning signals or weather conditions, only naming conventions, so it is related to PAGASA but does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: PAGASA gives local names to typhoons so Filipinos can easily identify them! These fun names come from a rotating list that is used again every few years.
copy.tl: Nagbibigay ang PAGASA ng mga lokal na pangalan sa mga bagyo para madali silang makilala ng mga Pilipino! Galing ang mga ito sa isang rotating list na ginagamit muli pagkalipas ng ilang taon.
copy.bis: Naghatag ang PAGASA og lokal nga ngalan sa mga bagyo aron dali silang mailhan sa mga Pilipino! Kini nga mga ngalan gikan sa usa ka rotating list nga gigamit usab matag pipila ka tuig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A red sunset means dry air from the west, so good weather is coming.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and record changes in the weather during a day or over some days and describe the different types and patterns of weather in the local area
assignedReviews.reason: The card presents a weather folklore prediction (red sky at night) rather than guiding students to observe and record weather changes over a day or days, or to describe local weather types and patterns. It shares the weather topic but does not directly support the competency's observational/recording skill.

copy.en: 'Red sky at night, sailor's delight' is true! A red sunset means dry air from the west, so good weather is coming.
copy.tl: 'Pulang langit sa gabi, magandang panahon bukas'—totoo! Ang pulang sunset ay senyales ng tuyong hangin mula sa kanluran, kaya magandang panahon ang paparating.
copy.bis: 'Pula nga langit sa gabii, maayong panahon ugma'—tinuod! Ang pula nga pagsalop nagpasabot sa mamala nga hangin gikan sa kasadpan, nagpahiyag sa maayong panahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The sharp edges of a rock weather faster than the middle, making big rocks smooth and rounded!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a weathering process that rounds boulders, but does not explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals. Weathering is a precursor to soil formation, but the card does not connect rock weathering to soil production, so it only shares the broad topic of weathering.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The sharp edges of a rock weather faster than the middle, making big rocks smooth and rounded!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a weathering effect on rocks but does not involve observing or collecting different rock types or describing similarities/differences in features such as texture, color, or grain crystal size. It is only tangentially related to rock observation.

copy.en: The sharp edges of a rock weather faster than the middle, making big rocks smooth and rounded!
copy.tl: Mas mabilis maweather ang matutulis na gilid ng bato kaysa gitna, kaya nagiging makinis at bilog ang malalaking bato!
copy.bis: Mas paspas mo-weather ang talinis nga ngilit sa bato kaysa tunga, busa mahimong hamis ug lingin ang dagkong mga bato!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: build their nests high up in tree branches and leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a tree habitat but does not use a drawing or diagram to classify Philippine animals/plants into terrestrial, aquatic, or aerial groups. It only states a single fact about weaver ants, so it does not directly support the classification skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: build their nests high up in tree branches and leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a list or draw up a table with examples of animals and plants in a particular habitat, such as a garden, rice field, seashore, and mangrove swamp
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not make a list or table of animals and plants in a named habitat. It only gives one example of an animal in a tree, without the required list/table format or multiple examples.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: build their nests high up in tree branches and leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows that weaver ants use trees as shelter (a basic need), but it does not identify the basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter) in a general way. It provides a single example of shelter, which is background knowledge rather than direct instruction on the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: build their nests high up in tree branches and leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies that weaver ants depend on trees (the environment) for shelter, but it does not explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet basic needs. It is a concrete example that could support the concept, but does not directly teach the dependency relationship.

copy.en: Weaver ants build their nests high up in tree branches and leaves — never on the ground!
copy.tl: Itinatayo ng mga hantik ang kanilang pugad sa mga sanga at dahon ng puno — hindi sa lupa!
copy.bis: Gitukod sa mga hantik ang ilang salag sa mga sanga ug dahon sa kahoy — dili sa yuta!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Weaverbirds often nest together in one tree
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: you'll see many hanging nests clustered side by side
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a list or draw up a table with examples of animals and plants in a particular habitat, such as a garden, rice field, seashore, and mangrove swamp
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not make a list or table of animals and plants in a named habitat.

copy.en: Weaverbirds often nest together in one tree, so you'll see many hanging nests clustered side by side!
copy.tl: Madalas maraming weaverbird ang sabay-sabay namumugad sa iisang puno, kaya makikita mo ang maraming pugad na nakabitin nang magkakatabi!
copy.bis: Kasagaran daghang weaverbird ang dungan nga nagsalag sa usa ka kahoy, mao nga makita nimo ang daghang nagbitay nga salag nga nag-abay!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Usually the male weaverbird builds the nest, and the female chooses him if she likes his finished nest.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes nest-building and mate choice, which are behaviors tied to reproduction, but it does not describe the characteristic of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) itself. It provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Usually the male weaverbird builds the nest, and the female chooses him if she likes his finished nest.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not identify which groups of animals give birth to live young versus lay eggs. It only mentions a bird's nest-building behavior, which is not the focus of the competency.

copy.en:
Which weaverbird builds the nest?

Usually the male weaverbird builds the nest, and the female chooses him if she likes his finished nest.
copy.tl:
Sino ang gumagawa ng pugad ng weaverbird?

Karaniwan ang lalaking weaverbird ang gumagawa ng pugad, at pinipili siya ng babae kung gusto niya ang nayaring pugad.
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang naghimo sa salag sa weaverbird?

Kasagaran ang laki nga weaverbird mao ang naghimo sa salag, ug ang baye mopili kaniya kon ganahan siya sa nahuman nga salag.

copy.bis: Ang West Valley Fault usa ka aktibo nga fault nga naa duol sa Metro Manila nga mahimong hinungdan sa kusog nga linog, mao nga kanayong andam!

copy.bis: Ganahan magdungan og salag ang mga tagak ug egret sa grupo sa mga kahoy — gitawag kini og heronry.

copy.bis: Sa nagpundo nga tubig sa lamakan motubo ang mga larva sa lamok una kini molupad.

copy.tl: Humihinga ang balyena sa pamamagitan ng butas sa ibabaw ng ulo nito na tinatawag na blowhole - kapag umaahon ito, lumalabas ang parang fountain ng hamog na tubig sa hangin.
copy.bis: Manginhawa ang balyena pinaagi sa lungag sa ibabaw sa iyang ulo nga gitawag og blowhole - kon mosulbong kini, moboso ang tubig pataas sa hangin.

copy.en: In Donsol, Sorsogon, so many whale sharks gather that it's become famous for watching them up close.
copy.tl: Sa Donsol, Sorsogon, napakaraming butanding ang nagtitipon kaya sikat itong puntahan para makita sila nang malapitan.
copy.bis: Sa Donsol, Sorsogon, daghan kaayong butanding ang nagtigom mao nga bantog kini nga adtoan aron makita sila og duol.

What's the largest fish in the world?

The whale shark is the largest fish in the entire world!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamalaking isda sa mundo?

Ang butanding o whale shark ang pinakamalaking isda sa buong mundo!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakadako nga isda sa kalibotan?

Ang tuki o whale shark mao ang pinakadako nga isda sa tibuok kalibotan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: drawn by plenty of plankton and fish eggs

copy.en: Whale sharks gather in Donsol, Sorsogon every year from November to June, drawn by plenty of plankton and fish eggs — and tourists get to swim with them safely.
copy.tl: Nagtitipon ang mga butanding sa Donsol, Sorsogon taun-taon mula Nobyembre hanggang Hunyo, dahil sa maraming plankton at itlog ng isda — at ligtas na nakakalangoy sila ng mga turista.
copy.bis: Nagtapok ang mga butanding sa Donsol, Sorsogon matag tuig gikan sa Nobyembre hangtod Hunyo, tungod sa daghang plankton ug itlog sa isda — ug luwas nga makalangoy uban kanila ang mga turista.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: extra-thick skin that acts like natural armor

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a physical adaptation (thick skin as armor) but does not frame it as an example of animals having 'changed to better suit their environment' nor does it involve mimicry or camouflage. assignedReviews.card_evidence: extra-thick skin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an outer body part (skin) but does not identify its role in movement or gathering food, which is the focus of the competency. Skin as armor is not about moving or feeding.

copy.en:
Why doesn't the whale shark get hurt easily?

Because the whale shark has extra-thick skin that acts like natural armor, protecting its whole body!
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi dali-daling masaktan ang butanding?

Dahil ang butanding ay may napakakapal na balat na parang natural na baluti, nagpoprotekta sa buong katawan nito!
copy.bis:
Nganong dili dali madaot ang butanding?

Tungod kay ang butanding adunay baga kaayo nga panit nga daw natural nga taming, nagpanalipod sa tibuok lawas niini!

copy.en:
Why do humpback whales sing the same song?

Male humpback whales sing long, complex songs, and all the males in one group sing the same song, which slowly changes over time — a kind of animal culture!
copy.tl:
Bakit magkatulad ang kanta ng mga humpback whale?

Ang mga lalaking humpback whale ay kumakanta ng mahaba at komplikadong kanta, at lahat ng lalaki sa isang grupo ay kumakanta ng parehong kanta na unti-unting nagbabago — isang uri ng kultura ng hayop!
copy.bis:
Nganong managsama ang awit sa mga humpback whale?

Ang mga lalaki nga humpback whale nagkanta og taas ug komplikadong mga awit, ug tanang lalaki sa usa ka grupo nagkanta sa mao rang awit nga hinay-hinay nagbag-o — usa ka porma sa kulturang hayop!

copy.en: A humpback whale sings a long, melodic song, while dolphins use fast clicks to hunt for food — one for talking, the other for finding dinner!
copy.tl: Mahaba at malumanay ang kanta ng humpback whale, habang gumagamit ang dolphin ng mabilis na 'click' para manghanap ng pagkain — para sa usapan ang isa, para sa paghahanap ang isa!
copy.bis: Taas ug malumo ang kanta sa humpback whale, samtang mogamit ang dolphin og paspas nga 'click' aron mangita og pagkaon — para sa panagsulti ang usa, para sa pagpangita ang usa!

copy.en:
What exactly is a plateau?

A plateau is a wide area of flat land that sits high above the land around it!
copy.tl:
Ano nga ba ang talampas?

Ang talampas ay isang malawak na lupang patag na nakaangat at mataas kaysa sa palibot nito!
copy.bis:
Unsa man gyud ang talampad?

Ang talampad mao ang lapad nga patag nga yuta nga taas ug habog kaysa sa palibot niini!

copy.bis: Ang adaptation usa ka kinaiya nga nagpauswag sa abilidad sa usa ka organismo nga mabuhi ug mosanay sa iyang palibot.

copy.en:
How do scientists start learning about something new?

They start by making observations, which means obtaining information using their senses like sight, hearing, and touch.
copy.tl:
Paano nagsisimula ang mga scientist na matuto tungkol sa isang bagong bagay?

Nagsisimula sila sa paggawa ng observation, ibig sabihin ay pagkuha ng impormasyon gamit ang kanilang mga senses tulad ng paningin, pandinig, at pandama.
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagsugod sa mga scientist ang pagkat-on mahitungod sa bag-ong butang?

Magsugod sila pinaagi sa paghimo og observation, nga nagpasabot sa pagkuha og impormasyon gamit ang ilang mga senses sama sa panan-aw, pandungog, ug paghikap.

When did Galileo discover the moons of Jupiter?

The famous scientist Galileo discovered the moons of Jupiter a long time ago in the year 1610!
copy.tl:
Kailan natuklasan ni Galileo ang mga buwan ng Jupiter?

Ang sikat na siyentipiko na si Galileo ay natuklas ng mga buwan ng Jupiter noong taong 1610!
copy.bis:
Kanus-a nadiskobre ni Galileo ang mga bulan sa Jupiter?

Ang bantog nga siyentipiko nga si Galileo nadiskobre sa mga bulan sa Jupiter niadtong tuig 1610!

When was the moon Titan discovered?

The amazing moon Titan was discovered a long time ago in the exact year 1655!
copy.tl:
Kailan natuklasan ang buwan na Titan?

Ang buwan na Titan ay natuklasan noong taong 1655! Ito ay isang napakagandang buwan sa kalawakan.
copy.bis:
Kanus-a nadiskobre ang bulan nga Titan?

Ang bulan nga Titan nadiskobre niadtong tuig 1655! Kini usa ka nindot nga bulan sa kalawakan.

copy.bis: Ang sedimentary nga bato kasagaran maporma duol sa ibabaw. Apan ang metamorphic ug kadaghanan sa igneous nga bato maporma sa mas lawom ug mainit nga ilawom!

Who discovered the two moons of Mars, Phobos and Deimos?

Asaph Hall discovered the two moons of Mars! Their names are Phobos and Deimos.
copy.tl:
Sino ang nakatuklas ng dalawang buwan ng Mars, ang Phobos at Deimos?

Si Asaph Hall ang nakatuklas ng dalawang buwan ng Mars! Ang mga pangalan nila ay Phobos at Deimos.
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang nakadiskobre sa duha ka bulan sa Mars, ang Phobos ug Deimos?

Si Asaph Hall ang nakadiskobre sa duha ka bulan sa Mars! Ang mga ngalan nila mao ang Phobos ug Deimos.

copy.tl: Noong 1932, sina John Cockcroft at Ernest Walton ang unang humati ng atom gamit ang isang makina!
copy.bis: Niadtong 1932, sila John Cockcroft ug Ernest Walton maoy unang nakabahin sa atom gamit ang makina!

Why does a cat lick itself?

A cat licks its own fur to clean itself — this removes dirt and tiny pests that could carry disease, keeping it healthy!

Bakit dinidilaan ng pusa ang sarili nito?

Dinidilaan ng pusa ang sariling balahibo para maglinis — tinatanggal nito ang dumi at maliliit na kuto na maaaring magdala ng sakit, para manatili itong malusog!
copy.bis:
Nganong gitilapan sa iring ang kaugalingon?

Gitilapan sa iring ang kaugalingong balhibo aron manghinlo — makuha niini ang hugaw ug gagmayng kuto nga makadala og sakit, aron magpabiling himsog!
